evidenceForCanonical: The CX map makes 19.01.05 the source and 19.01.03 the target of CX-05 (19.01-ticket-config-scaling-allocations-cx.md:14).

19.01.05:94 already recorded the direction of travel — 'the resolution ... is the CX-05 close-out. 19.01.03's own edge-case row for this now resolves to the same rule' — a sweep 19.01.03 never received.

19.01.03's own text was self-refuting: the same sentence claimed 'no per-ticket booking fee on the companion line' AND 'identical total structure to a comparable two-ticket general order', and its save-time check is equality against that two-ticket order. Only D-05's rule satisfies that check; zero-rating the companion makes the accessible pair strictly cheaper, breaking the stated parity test from the other side.

19.01.05 owns the companion entitlement as a concept (title, Behavior :27, happy path 5-8, entitlement default, COMPANION_ENTITLEMENT_EXCEEDED); 19.01.03 owns the fee model (types, basis, scope, rounding, splits), not the companion.

items.canonicalSource: none — no file in the tree states whether an RSVP carries a party size. The nearest ratified model is 19.03.01 D-05 (admission units) in the adjacent guest-list feature, which 19.11 cites for a different purpose but never adopts.
items.summary: 19.11 D-05 (cap counts heads, not RSVPs) and D-06/DT-03 (idempotent per Fan, one head per person, record keyed to the Fan's identity) admit two internally consistent readings of the 'Someone RSVPs for 6' edge case, and the tree picks neither. Resolving it decides whether a fan can bring five friends with one tap — a product behaviour, so classified OWNER and left unedited.
items.ownerBrief:
DECISION NEEDED — does a free-event RSVP carry guests, and if so how are they modelled?

WHAT IS ON DISK (19.11-rsvp-free-private-event-admission.md, status [PARTIAL]):
- D-02 (:113): 'RSVP issues a real admission record that scans, counts and closes like a ticket' — a name with no scannable artifact is the same failure as a comp with no barcode.
- D-05 (:116): 'The cap counts heads, not RSVPs' — context: 'Free events attract inflated party sizes'.
- D-06 (:117) + DT-03 (:93): 'RSVP is idempotent per Fan and self-releasable — one head per person'; 'the admission record is keyed to the Fan's identity (D-11: fans are real users, not CRM rows), so a repeat RSVP resolves to the same record'.
- Edge case (:56): '| Someone RSVPs for 6 | Free events attract inflated party sizes | Cap counts heads, not RSVPs (D-05) |'.

THE AMBIGUITY: the :56 row does not say whether RSVPing for six is allowed-and-counted-as-six, or refused-because-each-head-taps-for-itself. Both readings satisfy every decision in the file, and they build different products.

OPTION A — RSVP carries a party size (+N). One tap declares a party of six; six admission units come off the cap; six scannable records issue and land in the RSVPing Fan's wallet (19.12); idempotency applies to the entry rather than to each record.
  Pros: matches how free shows actually behave — people bring friends, and a group that cannot declare itself will show up anyway and break the count D-05 exists to protect. Reuses a model already ratified one sub-domain away: 19.03.01 D-05 — 'An allocation counts admission units (one body, one barcode); a +1 spends a unit and issues its own ticket; entry spend is atomic (no partial spend)' — with 19.03.01 DT-03 explicitly rejecting the alternative 'a +1 rides free on the named guest's ticket'. 19.11 already anchors D-02 to that family by citing 19.03.02 DT-01.
  Cons: the five guests are unidentified, which weakens D-06's identity keying and DT-03's stated de-dup mechanism; on a Producer's 20-cap private client playback one taker can consume a third of the room; and self-release becomes ambiguous (does one tap return one seat or six?).

OPTION B — no party size; every head RSVPs for itself. 'Cap counts heads' means the cap is denominated in heads and one tap can never claim six; a fan bringing friends forwards the link and each taps it.
  Pros: one record per identified human, which is exactly what D-06 and DT-03 specify and what makes the record keyable at all; self-release is unambiguous, and self-release is the only half of the DT-01 overbooking problem this feature can solve without no-show data; Invite-only and Private access modes keep their meaning because every attendee passes through the link.
  Cons: more friction for a group on an Open event; and the :56 edge-case row then has to state a refusal ('you cannot RSVP for six — send them the link') rather than reading as an allowance.

RECOMMENDATION: Option B for v1. It is what D-06 and DT-03 already describe, it keeps every admission record identity-keyed (which the door, the count and self-release all lean on), and the beachhead cases this feature was written for — a Producer's 20-person client session, an invite-only listening party — are named-invitee shaped anyway. If the owner wants groups on Open free events, adopt 19.03.01's admission-unit model verbatim rather than inventing a party-size attribute: that model is already ratified, already issues one barcode per body, and 19.03.01 DT-03 has already rejected the ride-free alternative.

WHAT THE ANSWER UNBLOCKS: 19.04 door scanning (do unidentified guest records scan, and against whose identity), 19.05.01 live count, 19.12 delivery (six passes into one wallet vs one each), 19.02.05 waitlist (a release returns one seat or six), and 19.03.02 Q-03, which asks whether comps may oversell 'as 19.11 proposes for RSVP'.

HOUSEKEEPING: 19.11 currently has no tracked question covering this — Q-01 is deliberate overbooking, Q-02 venue-less events, Q-03 the 07 boundary, Q-04 free-becomes-ticketed. Whichever way this lands, it should be written into D-05's wording and the :56 edge-case row, not only into a new decision, because :56 is where an implementer will look first.
